note: Progress metrics only; the reconstruction itself is not published here.

snapshot.subject: Promote codex-a06 (Wave A A06): strict closed cluster a06-skyquad-uvs-ltcg (+4 fn / +2,245 B)

categories.label: Shared-context rule (provisional)
categories.nature: Byte-identical. These functions sit in multi-function units whose only outside helpers are functions that were already verified; those helpers ride along unchanged as shared build context and are not counted a second time. The open question is the admission rule, not the bytes.
categories.plan: Gate rule under review. If it is tightened, the whole block can be taken out of the count in one step.

categories.label: Behaviour-verified (lower tier)
categories.nature: Not yet byte-proven. Each function was run side by side with the original on recorded inputs and gave the same results, with a control that is able to fail. Counted in the campaign figure on a lower proof tier; not part of the byte-exact tier.
categories.plan: Expected to be temporary: these are meant to be replaced by byte-exact versions as their units are rebuilt.

categories.label: Chosen local-variable names
categories.nature: Byte-identical. The period compiler orders some stack slots by the spelling of local variable names. Where no evidence names the original variable, a name was chosen that reproduces the layout.
categories.plan: Evidence-quality flag; revisit if naming evidence turns up.

categories.label: Invented helpers
categories.nature: Byte-identical. The source uses a small helper the original may not have had, for example a stand-in caller that gives the compiler the right surrounding context. The helper itself is never counted.
categories.plan: Evidence-quality flag; revisit and replace with the original structure where it can be identified.

categories.label: References to not-yet-named globals
categories.nature: Byte-identical, and every reference lands on the same address as in the original. The referenced global or function simply has no independently backed name yet.
categories.plan: Naming work; the bytes and addresses already agree.

categories.label: Older alignment annotation
categories.nature: Byte-identical, but the source reproduces the stack frame with an explicit alignment annotation. A later study of frame alignment suggests the original was written differently.
categories.plan: Grandfathered; due to be re-ported the newer way.

categories.label: Padded unit with verified context (provisional)
categories.nature: Byte-identical. A unit whose stack padding is reproduced by a mirror caller also uses an already verified helper with a custom register convention as uncounted build context.
categories.plan: Rule under review; one listed unit. Removable in one step.

categories.label: Array-constructor owner unit (provisional)
categories.nature: Byte-identical. The real owner of a compiler-generated array-construction helper is rebuilt together with its callers; the helper and one verified caller ride along as uncounted context, and four ownership controls are shown to fail when the arrangement is wrong.
categories.plan: Rule under review. Removable in one step.

categories.label: Single function exact only under whole-program optimisation (provisional)
categories.nature: Byte-identical. A single function with no custom register convention and no stack-frame demand that matches only when built with whole-program optimisation; switching that off, adding an ordinary caller and moving its data are all checked.
categories.plan: Rule under review; listed functions only. Removable in one step.

categories.label: Hand-written break test (provisional)
categories.nature: Byte-identical. The automatic one-character break test found nothing to change in these functions, so a committed hand-written edit inside the body is used instead and shown to break the match.
categories.plan: Rule under review; listed functions only. Removable in one step.

categories.label: Chosen local-variable names, checked class (provisional)
categories.nature: Byte-identical. In a few functions built without optimisation, the compiler orders stack slots by the spelling of the local variables. The names were chosen to reproduce the original layout. For each one, the same function with ordinary names is shown to differ only in that slot order, and the reason each chosen name lands where it does is recorded.
categories.plan: Becomes strict if the spelling-to-slot model predicts unseen functions correctly. Removable in one step.

categories.label: Unused local variables that fill the stack frame (provisional)
categories.nature: Byte-identical. In a few functions built without optimisation, the original stack frame holds bytes that no instruction ever touches. The rebuilt source declares unused locals to fill them. The compiler's own debug records confirm where each one lands, the original code is shown never to address that stretch, and removing any of them breaks the match. Their types and sizes are chosen; the original only shows that the space was there.
categories.plan: Becomes strict if the original locals are recovered or their type is shown to be forced. Removable in one step.

categories.label: Padded unit with rewritten-stack context (provisional)
categories.nature: Byte-identical. A padded unit uses an already verified helper, whose stack layout the compiler rewrote, as uncounted build context; building that helper differently is shown to break every caller.
categories.plan: Rule under review; one listed unit. Removable in one step.

categories.label: Context carried with its own stand-in (provisional)
categories.nature: Byte-identical. A verified helper rides along as uncounted context together with the stand-in it was itself verified with; the stand-in is shown to matter only for that helper, and the helper is shown to be needed.
categories.plan: Becomes strict once the helper matches without its stand-in, or a whole-program link re-proves it.

categories.label: Stand-in callers tied to the original (provisional)
categories.nature: Byte-identical. Some functions only take their original shape when a particular caller exists. Where that caller is not rebuilt yet, a clearly marked stand-in takes its place. Each stand-in copies a fact read from the original program, and removing it breaks exactly the functions that fact explains. Stand-ins are never counted.
categories.plan: Becomes strict as the real callers are rebuilt, or a whole-program link re-proves the unit. Removable in one step.

categories.label: Single function with its own stack realignment (provisional)
categories.nature: Byte-identical. A single function that realigns its own stack frame and matches only under whole-program optimisation; an aligned stand-in caller is shown to change it, as the original's callers would.
categories.plan: Becomes strict once a real caller is rebuilt with it, or a whole-program link re-proves it.

categories.label: Context that is not called directly (provisional)
categories.nature: Byte-identical. A verified helper that none of these functions calls rides along as uncounted context, because whole-program optimisation reads it through another link recorded from the original; removing it is shown to break the match.
categories.plan: Becomes strict once the unit holds every real caller, or a whole-program link re-proves it.

categories.label: Replaced records (provisional)
categories.nature: Byte-identical. A newer proof replaced an older record: either a larger unit that contains the old one, or a fresh proof for a record whose source had gone out of date. The old records are kept verbatim in a separate file; every function is counted once.
categories.plan: Rule under review. Deleting that one file returns the count to what it was before the rule.

exceptions.note: Apart from the behaviour-verified row, these flags describe how a unit was admitted or attributed (the evidence rules), not bytes that fail to match. A function can carry more than one flag, so the rows overlap and do not add up.
